: Provenance: CAPTURED against a real https://api.openai.com/v1/responses
: request, model gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18, a single `get_weather` tool, on
: 2026-08-20. This is the shape SMA-533's Task 12 was originally BLOCKED
: without: the stream conformance suite
: (tests/provider-stream-conformance/tests/conformance.rs, `openai_responses`
: module, `ToolCallCleanStop` scenario) needs a tool-call shape, and no
: capture existed anywhere in the repo -- deriving one from this crate's own
: unit tests instead of escalating is exactly how the FragmentedToolName
: Gemini fixture went wrong under SMA-522 (see that module's doc comment).
: This capture supersedes that risk for the Responses backend.
:
: Confirms `item_to_call` (backend/responses.rs) is correctly keyed on
: `item.id` (`fc_...`), not `call_id` (`call_...`): `output_item.added`
: carries both, separately, and `function_call_arguments.delta` carries only
: `item_id`. Also confirms arguments stream as multiple small fragments
: (`{"`, `city`, `":"`, `Berlin`, `"}`) rather than arriving whole, and that
: `response.completed` reports `"status":"completed"` with
: `"incomplete_details":null` for a turn whose only output is a function
: call -- the shape that exposed `terminal_events` reporting `Finish{Stop}`
: instead of `Finish{ToolCalls}` for a tool-only turn (fixed in the same
: SMA-533 PR that adds this fixture; see `ResponsesTranslator`'s tests
: module, and `tool_call_turn_finishes_with_tool_calls` in
: `responses_streaming.rs`, which exercises this exact fixture end to end).
:
: `event:` lines are kept, unlike this directory's other `responses_*.txt`
: fixtures. Those omit them; async-openai's `ResponseStreamEvent` is
: `#[serde(tag = "type")]`, so the parser dispatches purely off the JSON
: `type` key inside `data:` and the `event:` line is cosmetic to it -- but
: this fixture is a literal transcription of a real capture that DID send
: them, and (per this crate's `anthropic`-sibling module's own reasoning
: for the same choice in the stream conformance suite) a fixture claiming
: to be CAPTURED should stay faithful to what the wire actually sent, not
: just to what the parser happens to need.
:
: Three kinds of trimming from the raw capture, all deliberate:
:
: 1. `response.created` and `response.in_progress` are dropped.
:    `ResponsesTranslator::consume` has no arm for either (both fall through
:    to the trailing `other` debug-log arm), and every fixture already
:    committed in this directory starts at the first translator-relevant
:    event for the same reason (compare `responses_reasoning_then_text.txt`).
:
: 2. Every delta in the raw capture also carried an `"obfuscation"` field --
:    an opaque per-chunk padding string OpenAI adds to streaming responses
:    (documented at platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/responses-streaming
:    as anti-side-channel padding, not response data). It has no
:    corresponding field on `ResponseFunctionCallArgumentsDeltaEvent` to
:    deserialize into -- deserialization tolerates it silently either way,
:    since none of these event structs are `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`
:    -- but it carries no semantic content and is not stable API surface,
:    so it is dropped here for the same reason this directory's other
:    fixtures already omit every optional field the translator does not
:    read (no `logprobs`, no `metadata`, a minimal `output`).
:
: 3. `response.completed`'s `.response` object is reduced from the 35 keys
:    the raw capture sends to the 8 this fixture keeps (`created_at`, `id`,
:    `incomplete_details`, `model`, `object`, `output`, `status`, `usage`)
:    -- the same "only what the translator reads" convention as (1) and (2)
:    above, and as `responses_reasoning_then_text.txt`. This is NOT a "two
:    omissions" story: the other 27 keys are absent from this fixture but
:    present on the real wire, and their absence here should not be read
:    as absence there. For the record, they are: `background`,
:    `completed_at`, `error`, `frequency_penalty`, `instructions`,
:    `max_output_tokens`, `max_tool_calls`, `metadata`, `moderation`,
:    `parallel_tool_calls`, `presence_penalty`, `previous_response_id`,
:    `prompt_cache_key`, `prompt_cache_retention`, `reasoning`,
:    `safety_identifier`, `service_tier`, `store`, `temperature`, `text`,
:    `tool_choice`, `tool_usage`, `tools`, `top_logprobs`, `top_p`,
:    `truncation`, and `user`. The same trimming happens one level deeper:
:    the raw capture's `usage.input_tokens_details` carries both
:    `cached_tokens` and `cache_write_tokens`; this fixture keeps only
:    `cached_tokens`. OpenAI does send `cache_write_tokens` on the wire --
:    it just is not consumed by the translator, so it is not reproduced
:    here. Don't read its absence from this file as evidence OpenAI omits
:    it.
